# Testing modules and HTTP

Documentation route: /docs/testing/modules

Test HTTP behavior through a real router and replace providers when a test needs controlled data. Start with the generated feature tests, then use overrides for external dependencies.

Enable the runtime's optional test helpers only for development:

```toml
[dev-dependencies]
xecute = { version = "0.1.8", features = ["testing"] }
```

Generated manifests already include this entry. `TestingModule` compiles isolated
containers, applies overrides before initialization, and validates the final
dependency graph. Unknown or repeated overrides are errors, preventing a silently
unused mock. Values replace the same registered Rust type; for trait-based mocks,
use a concrete adapter containing `Arc<dyn YourTrait>` and replace that adapter.
Production containers remain unchanged.

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use xecute::testing::{TestApp, TestingModule};

let mut module = TestingModule::new();
for definition in crate::app_module::AppModule::definitions() {
    module = module.module(definition);
}
// Example: module = module.override_value(DatabaseGateway(Arc::new(FakeDatabase)));
let container = Arc::new(module.compile()?);
let routes = crate::app_module::AppModule::router_with_container(container)?;
let app = TestApp::new(crate::server::router(routes, &crate::configs::Config::default()));

let response = app.post("/example")
    .json(&serde_json::json!({"name": "Example"}))
    .send().await?
    .assert_status(axum::http::StatusCode::CREATED);
let body: serde_json::Value = response.json()?;
```

Run these async helpers inside a Tokio runtime, such as `#[tokio::test]`.
The client runs the actual Router and middleware without a socket. It supports
arbitrary HTTP methods through `.request`, common method helpers, raw bodies,
headers, JSON payloads, and `.peer(SocketAddr)` for limiter tests. Loopback peer
information is supplied by default. Responses expose status, headers, bounded
bytes, typed JSON, and chainable `.assert_status`/`.assert_json` methods. Invalid
requests return test errors rather than panicking. Request and body collection
have a five-second timeout and a 1 MiB response limit; adjust with
`TestApp::timeout` and `response_limit`. This tests HTTP behavior in-process;
network/TLS/deployment behavior still belongs in deployment smoke tests.

The generated `src/tests/application.rs` demonstrates isolated container startup
and safe mapped errors. Resource tests demonstrate JSON validation and storage
through the same test client. The runtime test suite also covers trait adapters,
mock isolation, concurrent initialization, nested request scopes, and cleanup.

# Runnable examples

Documentation route: /docs/testing/examples

Run these commands from the repository root. Each example is implemented under
`xecute/examples`; the associated tests compile its application setup. Clone the repository to run
these examples; applications can enable the same APIs through their Cargo features.

| Example | Command | Requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Module imports and request inputs | `cargo run -p xecute --example module_imports` | HTTP port 3000 |
| Async resource lifecycle | `cargo run -p xecute --example async_lifecycle` | No external service |
| PostgreSQL repository/transactions | `cargo run -p xecute --example postgres --features postgres` | Development `DATABASE_URL` |
| JWT guards and permissions | `cargo run -p xecute --example auth --features auth` | Random `JWT_SECRET` of at least 32 bytes; port 3000 |
| Worker with TTL cache | `cargo run -p xecute --example jobs_cache --features jobs,cache` | No external service |
| CQRS buses and event subscribers | `cargo run -p xecute --example cqrs --features cqrs` | HTTP port 3000 |
| Validated private file upload | `cargo run -p xecute --example file_upload --features upload` | Private temporary storage; port 3000 |

Run one HTTP example at a time when using the same listening port. Read each
example's module/controller comments for curl commands and behavioral details.
The PostgreSQL example runs migrations and inserts data; use its disposable setup.

## Focused checks

```sh
cargo test -p xecute --example module_imports
cargo test -p xecute --features testing --test async_lifecycle
cargo test -p xecute --features auth --test auth_http --test guards_http --example auth
cargo test -p xecute --features jobs,cache,testing --test jobs --test cache --example jobs_cache
cargo test -p xecute --features cqrs,testing --test cqrs --example cqrs
```

## External-service suites

The [PostgreSQL guide](skills/xecute/references/integrations/postgres.md) and
[Redis cache guide](skills/xecute/references/integrations/cache.md) explain disposable services and
credentials. Live tests are ignored in the normal suite and fail clearly when
explicitly invoked without the required environment variable.

```sh
# Dedicated database; role needs permission to create test databases:
cargo test -p xecute --features postgres,testing --test postgres -- --ignored

# Dedicated Redis instance; tests use separate random namespaces:
cargo test -p xecute --features cache-redis --test cache_redis -- --ignored
```

Set `TEST_DATABASE_URL` or `TEST_REDIS_URL` as described in those guides before
running the corresponding command. Repository CI has explicit database/Redis
service jobs. No live credential is stored in the docs.

## Documentation snippets versus complete applications

Guide snippets show the relevant API or integration fragment. They are not always
complete standalone programs. For executable application boundaries, use the
complete examples and generated-app tests. A code block documenting a placeholder
attribute does not make it an operational lifecycle/interceptor feature.

# Deployment

Documentation route: /docs/operations/deployment

Deploy a generated application after it builds and passes tests locally. Follow the release/container instructions and supply your own production configuration and secrets.

From a generated application using registry dependencies:

```sh
docker build --tag my-app:local .
docker run --rm --name my-app \
  --read-only --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt=no-new-privileges \
  --pids-limit=128 --memory=512m --cpus=1 --stop-timeout=15 \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 my-app:local
```

The Dockerfile builds a stripped static musl binary for amd64 or arm64 and runs
it in `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot`. Its container listener defaults
to `0.0.0.0:3000`. The final image contains no build tools, shell, package manager,
or curl. Configure HTTP health probes in the orchestrator.

Pass runtime configuration through environment variables or the deployment's
secret mechanism. `.env` is excluded from source control and the Docker context.
Allow a stop timeout longer than `SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`. Local runtime path
dependencies require a custom Docker build context. Native dependencies must
support static musl linking if you retain the generated build configuration.

Replace in-memory repositories with durable storage, add application-specific
authentication/authorization, and terminate TLS at your ingress. Add readiness
checks for external dependencies when introducing them.

# Troubleshooting

Documentation route: /docs/operations/troubleshooting

Find the symptom closest to yours in the table below. Read the full command output first, and check whether you are in the generated application or the Xecute repository.

| Symptom | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Installed CLI lacks `run dev` or middleware support | Update to CLI 0.1.7 or later and use runtime/macros 0.1.5 or later |
| Generated app cannot find `Application` | Update its runtime/macros to 0.1.5 or later |
| Locked build says the lockfile must change | Run `cargo generate-lockfile`, review it, and commit the result |
| Generator cannot register a resource | Run from the project root and retain the `// xecute:` markers in `app_module.rs` |
| Resource already exists | Choose another feature name or edit the existing feature; generators do not overwrite it |
| Middleware annotation produces an ordering error | Place it below the owning `#[controller]` or `#[routes]` macro |
| Wrong payload reaches a manually invoked handler | Automatic validation occurs through the generated HTTP extractor, not arbitrary Rust method calls |
| Browser cross-origin requests fail | Configure exact `cors.origins` plus the required methods and headers |
| Many clients share a rate-limit quota | Check whether a reverse proxy is the direct socket peer |
| Stored records disappear after restart | The generated repository is in memory; add durable storage |
| Container cannot resolve a local runtime dependency | Use registry dependencies or adapt the Docker build context |

## Keep learning

[Scope and limitations](skills/xecute/references/operations/limitations.md). Return to the [learning path](skills/xecute/references/index.md) whenever you need a different topic.

# Scope and limitations

Documentation route: /docs/operations/limitations

Check this page before planning around a capability. It separates generated behavior from features you must implement or configure in your application.

Xecute provides DI, module metadata, controller adapters, validation, HTTP
middleware, API documentation, and starter application infrastructure. It does
not currently generate database-backed repositories, complete CRUD operations,
login/session scaffolding, broker transports, or event sourcing. Optional
SQLx PostgreSQL integration supports lifecycle-managed pools, migrations, and native
transactions; see the [PostgreSQL guide](skills/xecute/references/integrations/postgres.md).

The middleware API implements app, controller, and route scopes. `#[module]`
describes DI boundaries and does not automatically attach HTTP middleware.
Executable guards support application, controller, and route policies. Optional
JWT authentication and role/permission checks are documented in the
[authentication guide](skills/xecute/references/integrations/auth.md). Optional [background jobs](skills/xecute/references/integrations/jobs.md)
provide bounded process-local workers and interval schedules; [TTL caching](skills/xecute/references/integrations/cache.md)
supports memory and Redis backends. Optional [CQRS buses](skills/xecute/references/integrations/cqrs.md)
provide typed command/query dispatch, event fan-out and shared pipelines; direct
handler CQRS remains supported. Reserved attribute markers, including
interceptors, lifecycle attributes, and exception decorators, are not complete
execution systems. Async lifecycle
behavior is available through explicit provider registration methods:
`singleton_async`, `on_init`, and `on_shutdown`; await `initialize_async` before
serving and `shutdown_async` after request draining. See the
[runtime lifecycle guide](skills/xecute/references/architecture/lifecycle.md).

Licensed under **Apache-2.0**.

## Keep learning

[Choose your next guide](skills/xecute/references/index.md). Return to the [learning path](skills/xecute/references/index.md) whenever you need a different topic.

# Cargo feature reference

Documentation route: /docs/reference/features

The runtime's default feature set is empty. Enable only the optional modules used
by your application. Async lifecycle, DI, controllers, custom guards, middleware,
configuration, error envelopes and versioning are part of the base runtime.

| Flag | Enables | Required setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth` | JWT verification, verified principal and role/permission policies | Trusted key/issuer/audience and guards |
| `postgres` | SQLx PostgreSQL pool/migrations/transactions | URL, migrations and repository/provider registration |
| `jobs` | In-process workers and interval scheduling | Queue limits, handlers and lifecycle draining |
| `cache` | Bounded memory TTL/LRU cache | Explicit keys, value limits and TTLs |
| `cache-redis` | Redis backend; includes `cache` | Redis URL, namespace, timeout and provider |
| `cqrs` | Typed command/query/event buses and behaviors | Typed messages/handlers and configured registries |
| `testing` | Isolated TestingModule and in-process HTTP client | Usually enable in dev-dependencies |
| `upload` | Streaming multipart and private local storage | Upload policy/storage and HTTP body limits |
| `upload-s3` | S3 storage adapter; includes `upload` | Bucket/region and trusted AWS configuration |

## Enable features in your application

Add the flags you need to the runtime dependency. Keep the same dependency version
in normal and dev dependencies; enable `testing` for test helpers.

```toml
[dependencies]
xecute = { version = "0.1", features = ["auth", "cqrs"] }

[dev-dependencies]
xecute = { version = "0.1", features = ["testing"] }
```

Cargo unifies feature selections for the same dependency source. Keep runtime and
dev-dependency sources consistent. In generated workspaces, declare the source in
`[workspace.dependencies]` and select app/test features through inherited entries.

## Unsupported assumptions

Feature flags expose runtime APIs; they do not automatically add configured
modules, change controller flow, create database tables or protect endpoints.
There are no ORM-specific Diesel/SeaORM/MongoDB flags, WebSocket gateways, remote
message transports, automatic HTTP cache decorators or persisted cron/saga
features in this implementation. Compose other Rust libraries explicitly when
those capabilities are required.

The docs validation script compares this table with the actual runtime manifest
so stale or invented flag names are caught during documentation checks.

---

# Release process

Documentation route: /docs/reference/releases

This page is for maintainers publishing Xecute packages. Application users normally want the CLI update guide instead.

See [CHANGELOG.md](skills/xecute/references/reference/changelog.md) for version-by-version changes and
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/morshedulmunna/xecute/releases) for published
release notes. Git tags alone do not create GitHub Release pages.

Maintain an `## [VERSION] - YYYY-MM-DD` section in `CHANGELOG.md` before releasing.
Publish the crate, then push the matching CLI tag, such as `v0.1.10`. The
[release workflow](https://github.com/morshedulmunna/xecute/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml) copies that exact changelog
section into the GitHub Release body and adds the versioned installation command.
It creates a missing release or updates the notes of an existing release without
moving its source tag. Historical CLI tags can be backfilled through the
workflow's **Run workflow** input.

Changelog/workflow changes on `main` also synchronize the latest changelog
version when its tag already exists; an untagged future version is deferred.
This initializes the existing latest release when release automation is first
added. It does not publish crates or create version tags automatically.

Preview the release body locally:

```sh
python3 scripts/release_notes.py --tag v0.1.10 --output /tmp/xecute-release-notes.md
```

When manually using GitHub's **Create a new release** page, **Generate release
notes** uses the PR-label categories in [.github/release.yml](https://github.com/morshedulmunna/xecute/blob/main/.github/release.yml).
For the curated notes in this repository, use the changelog-backed workflow or
paste the corresponding changelog section into the release description.

[Changelog](skills/xecute/references/reference/changelog.md). Return to the [learning path](skills/xecute/references/index.md) whenever you need a different topic.

# Changelog

Documentation route: /docs/reference/changelog

Review changes before updating an existing application. Updating the CLI does not rewrite generated application files.

Changes are grouped by published CLI version, newest first. Runtime and macro
versions are listed when they changed alongside a CLI release. Updating the CLI
does not rewrite existing application source; generator changes apply to newly
created projects and resources.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.1.20] - 2026-10-27

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.20`, `xecute 0.1.10`, and `xmacros 0.1.8`.

### Changed

- Resolve a fresh lockfile with the latest compatible dependencies when creating
  standalone MVC/CQRS applications, including local-runtime projects. Report
  resolution failures with retry instructions instead of copying a bundled snapshot.
- Mount generated features through their module routers. Support module-level
  `#[guard(...)]`, `guards = [...]`, roles and permissions alongside controller and
  route policies, with ordered execution and request-scoped DI context.
- Publish the redesigned dark documentation site, guided tutorials, and downloadable
  AI-agent skill bundle with synchronized topic references and a complete manual.


### Added

- Optional typed CommandBus/QueryBus dispatch and observable EventBus fan-out,
  with immutable registrations, shared execution behaviors, explicit typed context,
  DI scope/module validation, cancellation ownership, and safe panic reports.
- Add a complete HTTP CQRS example with separate DTOs and event subscribers,
  an adoption/architecture guide, and routing/pipeline/DI/failure/cancellation tests.

- Optional bounded in-process background queues with receipts, retry/timeout
  policies, panic isolation, graceful draining and fixed-interval schedules.
- Optional bounded memory TTL/LRU cache and namespaced Redis cache, with explicit
  invalidation, safe errors and lifecycle cleanup. Add a worker/cache example,
  guides, deterministic unit tests, and live Redis CI coverage.

- Executable application/controller/route guards and additive role/permission
  policies. Add optional pinned HS256/RS256 bearer authentication, verified-user
  extraction, DI-backed verifier resolution, and safe 401/403 responses.
- Add an authentication guide and runnable demo, real signature and HTTP tests,
  and macro checks for invalid/empty authorization declarations.

- Optional SQLx PostgreSQL integration with validated/redacted configuration,
  lifecycle-managed connection pools, startup migrations, readiness checks, and
  native transactions. Include a module/repository example, setup/deployment
  documentation, and live PostgreSQL CI tests.

- Async singleton factories with dependency-ordered `initialize_async`, async
  startup/cleanup hooks, and explicit reverse-order `shutdown_async`.
- Serialize lifecycle calls across container clones, roll back failed startup,
  preserve dependency validation across await points, and support cancellation
  recovery through explicit shutdown.
- Add `TestingModule::compile_async`, a runnable lifecycle example, and tests for
  ordering, concurrency, failures, cancellation, overrides, and validation.

## [0.1.19] - 2026-10-27

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.19`, unchanged `xecute 0.1.9` and `xmacros 0.1.7`.

### Changed

- Generate CQRS resources as controller → command/query handler → repository.
  Handlers inject the shared repository directly; create handlers retain name
  normalization. Remove the mandatory forwarding service and its registrations.
  MVC resources retain controller → service → repository. Existing apps are not
  rewritten automatically.

## [0.1.18] - 2026-10-27

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.18`, unchanged `xecute 0.1.9` and `xmacros 0.1.7`.

### Added

- Include module imports/exports guidance and an imports section in both MVC and
  CQRS resource module templates.
- Document controller inputs in both resource templates: validated JSON, path
  parameters, query strings, headers, cookies, forms, text, bytes, middleware
  extensions, connection info, and multipart uploads, with handler examples.
- Add a runnable module-import example demonstrating exported service injection,
  request extraction, validation, and HTTP checks in the source repository.

## [0.1.17] - 2026-10-24

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.17`, `xecute 0.1.9`, and `xmacros 0.1.7`.
Runtime and macro releases update documentation and package descriptions only.

### Documentation

- Describe Xecute consistently as application architecture tools and macros built
  on Axum, rather than a separate framework, across READMEs, generated project
  documentation, crate descriptions, and crate-level documentation.

### Fixed

- Initialize versioning configuration directly in generated root-route tests so
  Clippy passes with `--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.

## [0.1.16] - 2026-10-24

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.16`, unchanged `xecute 0.1.8` and `xmacros 0.1.6`.

### Changed

- Emit only the `server listening` startup log. Serve the bound address, local URL,
  enabled Swagger/OpenAPI and versioned documentation paths, and static mount at
  `GET /` instead of announcing each endpoint in separate logs.

### Fixed

- Generate shared lint policies in `[workspace.lints]` and only
  `[lints] workspace = true` in workspace apps, preserving root lint customizations.

## [0.1.15] - 2026-10-24

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.15`, unchanged `xecute 0.1.8` and `xmacros 0.1.6`.

### Changed

- Generate workspace tooling, Git settings, Docker ignore rules, and GitHub
  configuration once at the root rather than duplicating them in each app.

- Centralize generated workspace dependency versions and paths in the root
  `[workspace.dependencies]`. Apps inherit dependencies with `workspace = true`,
  retaining their own feature selections and test-only runtime features.
- Adding apps and generating resources preserves existing shared dependency
  definitions. Explicit app runtime paths update the shared workspace runtime.

## [0.1.14] - 2026-10-24

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.14`, unchanged `xecute 0.1.8` and `xmacros 0.1.6`.

### Added

- `xecute new <project|.> --workspace` scaffolds a Cargo workspace with its first
  application under `apps/`, a shared lockfile, tooling, and workspace CI.
- `xecute g apps <app_name>` and `xecute generate apps <app_name>` add applications
  that inherit the workspace architecture, with `--mvc` and `--cqrs` overrides.
- Workspace applications retain feature modules, application configuration,
  static files, resource generators, tests, and Dockerfiles built from the
  workspace root. Local runtime paths can be inherited or overridden.
- Integration coverage for workspace membership, default MVC, CQRS selection,
  resource generation, architecture overrides, in-place creation, and conflicts.

### Changed

- MVC remains the default architecture for new projects and workspaces.
- Resolve newly added workspace members while retaining existing locked
  dependency versions.

## [0.1.13] - 2026-10-23

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.13`, `xecute 0.1.8`, and unchanged `xmacros 0.1.6`.

### Added

- Runnable file-upload controller example with private local storage, multipart
  OpenAPI metadata, size/type validation, and HTTP persistence/error tests.

### Changed

- Move generated application settings to config/AppConfig.toml, updating startup,
  Docker, and documentation paths.

- New projects generate only v1; remove the built-in v2 example and uploads module,
  upload configuration, and default upload/S3 features. Runtime upload and versioning
  APIs remain available for custom modules.

## [0.1.12] - 2026-10-23

Packages: `xecute-cli 0.1.12`, `xecute 0.1.7`, and `xmacros 0.1.6`.

### Added

- Streaming multipart uploads with actual size/count limits, MIME signature checks,
  private staging, generated keys, checksums, local atomic storage, optional official
  AWS S3 storage, and handled-failure batch rollback.
- Explicit /v1 and /v2 route groups with independently validated OpenAPI contracts,
  version-specific Swagger pages, and generated upload/version examples.
- Cargo feature selection through `xecute run dev --features`, plus optional S3
  container builds and configuration in AppConfig.toml with credentials kept outside TOML.

- Typed environment configuration with required/optional values, conversion, defaults,
  numeric bounds, JSON parsing, custom invariants, and redacted secret/error handling.
- Safe runtime exception envelopes and explicit domain-error mappings retained by
  generated middleware, with request correlation and protected internal failures.
- Automatic per-request DI contexts and controller routing; nested request/transient
  resolution, concurrent singleton caching, eager startup initialization, and graph validation.
- Optional testing helpers: isolated module/provider overrides, in-process HTTP client,
  JSON assertions, response size bounds, timeouts, and generated usage examples.

### Changed

- Ordinary generated application settings now load from required AppConfig.toml;
  .env is optional and contains only secret examples. TOML types/unknown keys are
  validated at startup, and the same snapshot configures server and logging.

- Generated applications use runtime 0.1.7 and macros 0.1.6 APIs. These package
  versions are published alongside CLI 0.1.12.
- Provider construction errors are cached per scope; undeclared factory dependencies
  and missing required registrations now fail explicitly.


### Fixed

- Serve a generated static landing page at both `/static` and `/static/`.

## [0.1.11] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- A shared environment reader reused by generated server and logging configuration.

- Default public static file serving with a generated example, GET/HEAD/range support, and private-path rejection.
- JSON console/file logging using only LOG_STDOUT_ENABLED and LOG_FILE_DIR, with built-in daily rotation, retention, and shutdown flushing.
- A composable tracing exporter layer hook for future cloud logging integrations.
- A repository changelog and GitHub Release automation using the matching version
  section as release notes.

## [0.1.10] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- `GET /` welcome JSON with HTTP 200, the application name, status, and the Swagger
  documentation path when enabled.
- Startup logs with server, Swagger UI, and OpenAPI URLs using the actual bound
  port, including OS-assigned ports.
- Browser-usable loopback URLs for wildcard bindings and bracketed IPv6 addresses.
- Tests for the welcome response, disabled Swagger, and startup URL formatting.

### Changed

- Disabled Swagger is explicitly logged; the welcome response does not advertise
  a documentation link when it is disabled.

### Fixed

- Fresh applications no longer return `Route not found` at `/`. Other unregistered
  paths continue to return the normal 404 error envelope.

## [0.1.9] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- CQRS `services/<feature>_service.rs` for shared business operations. Command and
  query handlers inject the service, which injects the repository.
- Service provider registration and exports in generated CQRS modules.

### Changed

- New resources and standalone building blocks live under `src/modules/<feature>/`.
- `src/modules/mod.rs` declares features; application registration uses
  `crate::modules::<feature>`.
- Resource HTTP tests live inside the feature at `tests/http.rs`; shared server
  tests remain in `src/tests/`.
- Rust scaffolding templates use `.rs` instead of `.tmpl`, preventing their
  classification as Go Template. The manifest template uses `Cargo.toml.in`.

## [0.1.8] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- `xecute update` and `xecute uninstall`, targeting the running executable's
  Cargo installation root, including custom installation roots.
- `xecute new .` for in-place initialization and `--name` for an explicit package name.
- Preflight collision and symlink checks before in-place scaffold writes.
- Cargo failure reporting and Windows helper handling for executable replacement
  or removal after the running CLI exits.

### Changed

- Removed framework-comparison wording from package descriptions and documentation.
- Generated applications use runtime `xecute 0.1.6`; macros remain `xmacros 0.1.5`.
- Existing application files are retained during CLI management operations.

## [0.1.7] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- `xecute run dev` with automatic debug rebuild/restart, debouncing, and recovery
  after compiler errors.
- `--bin`, repeatable `--watch`, and application argument forwarding after `--`.
- Source/configuration and `.env` watching with build-output exclusions, including
  custom Cargo target directories.
- Managed process-tree shutdown on restarts and Ctrl-C.
- App-level `Application::use_middleware` and controller/route `#[middleware(...)]`.
- Ordered middleware execution, early responses, and a global `src/middleware.rs`
  configuration hook.

### Changed

- Generated applications use runtime `xecute 0.1.5` and macros `xmacros 0.1.5`.

## [0.1.6] - 2026-10-23

### Added

- MVC generation by default, explicit `--mvc`, and opt-in CQRS through `--cqrs`.
- Persistent architecture selection in `.xecute/architecture` for later generators.
- CQRS create-command and list-query handlers with automatic DI registration.

### Changed

- Request validation uses `validator` instead of `garde`, automatically rejecting
  invalid body/query DTOs before controller business logic runs.
- Repository metadata points to `morshedulmunna/xecute`.
- Added a root workspace manifest and build documentation.
- Generated applications use runtime `xecute 0.1.4` and macros `xmacros 0.1.4`.

# AI agent skills

Documentation route: /docs/skills/ai-agent

Give your AI coding agent the same documentation you use. The Xecute skill teaches
it the project structure, MVC/CQRS conventions, request validation, module guards,
integrations, and verification workflow.

## Download the complete skill

[Download the Xecute skill bundle](/skills/xecute.zip)

The ZIP contains one `xecute/` folder:

```text
xecute/
├── SKILL.md                 # Entry point and application conventions
└── references/
    ├── topics.md             # All topics, grouped by task
    ├── full.md              # Complete documentation in one file
    ├── getting-started/     # Tutorials and request flow
    ├── architecture/        # Modules, DI, scopes and lifecycle
    ├── http/                # Controllers, validation, errors and files
    ├── integrations/        # PostgreSQL, JWT, jobs, cache and CQRS
    └── ...                  # CLI, configuration, tests and operations
```

All topic references are included. The agent can read the complete manual or load
only the pages relevant to its task. The bundle is generated from the maintained
docs, so its content stays aligned with this site.

## Install for your agent

1. Download and extract the ZIP.
2. Move the `xecute` folder into your agent's skills directory. For Codex, use
   `~/.codex/skills/xecute/` (or `$CODEX_HOME/skills/xecute/` when configured).
3. Start a new agent session so it can discover the skill.
4. Open your application repository and ask the agent to use the skill.

Other agents can use the Markdown references directly, even if they use a
different skill installation format. Follow that agent's own skill conventions.

Example prompt:

```text
Use $xecute to add a user feature to this application.
Read its existing architecture and the relevant Xecute references first.
Keep controllers thin, put DTOs in dto/, and add HTTP tests for the behavior.
```

To study the whole framework:

```text
Read the Xecute skill and references/full.md.
Explain this project's architecture, then use the relevant topic guides
when implementing the next task. Check the installed APIs before making changes.
```

## Read without installing

| Resource | Best for |
| --- | --- |
| [SKILL.md](/skills/xecute/SKILL.md) | Inspect the agent instructions |
| [Topic index](/llms.txt) | Discover every machine-readable page |
| [Full documentation](/llms-full.txt) | Read all documentation in one request |
| [Bundled reference index](/skills/xecute/references/topics.md) | Browse the skill's included files |

These URLs return plain text or Markdown and do not require JavaScript. Resolve
them relative to the documentation site's base path when hosted in a subdirectory.
Downloading only SKILL.md does not include its references; use the complete ZIP
for an offline skill.

## What the skill helps the agent do

- Follow MVC or CQRS already selected by your application.
- Register module definitions, providers, exports and guarded module routers.
- Keep body/query/path inputs and DTO validation in the right layer.
- Configure optional integrations and lifecycle cleanup explicitly.
- Test route behavior, authorization, persistence boundaries and failures.

The skill supplies guidance, not permission to publish or deploy. Your task and
repository instructions still control what the agent should change. Match the
reference examples to the dependency versions installed in your application.
